label: Bonus Class 1
title: Two Letters, One Sound: Digraphs
bigIdea: English has about 44 sounds but only 26 letters, so it often uses two letters to write one sound: sh, ch, th, ck, ph and wh. A spelling detective counts sounds, not letters.
bigIdeaAr: في الإنجليزية نحو 44 صوتاً لكن 26 حرفاً فقط، لذلك تستخدم أحياناً حرفين لكتابة صوت واحد: sh و ch و th و ck و ph و wh. محقق التهجئة يعدّ الأصوات لا الحروف.
builtOn: Lessons 1-4: Hello / thank you / How old are you? / This is my... / He is... She is... (brother, sister)
Phonics Lesson 1: j, v, w, x, y, z
Phonics Lesson 3: digraphs sh and ch (ship, fish, chip, chair)
Preview only (taught later): th in Lesson 5; ck, ph and wh are met in reading across the level

objectives.en: I can explain what a digraph is: two letters that make one sound.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أشرح ما هو الحرف المزدوج: حرفان يصنعان صوتاً واحداً.

objectives.en: I can count the sounds in a word like ship (3 sounds, 4 letters).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أعدّ الأصوات في كلمة مثل ship (3 أصوات و4 حروف).

objectives.en: I can hear the two sounds of th: think (like ث) and this (like ذ).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أسمع صوتي th: في think (مثل الثاء) وفي this (مثل الذال).

objectives.en: I can find sh, ch, th, ck, ph and wh in words and read them.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أجد sh و ch و th و ck و ph و wh في الكلمات وأقرأها.

keyTerms.meaning: Two letters that make one sound: sh in ship.
What you hear. We count sounds with our fingers.
What you see and write. A word can have more letters than sounds.
Your throat buzzes when you say it: th in this.
Only air, no buzz: th in think.

facts.en: English borrowed the Latin (Roman) alphabet, which has 26 letters. But English has about 44 sounds. So English pairs letters up to write the missing sounds.
facts.ar: استعارت الإنجليزية الأبجدية اللاتينية ذات الـ26 حرفاً، لكن في الإنجليزية نحو 44 صوتاً، لذلك تجمع حرفين معاً لتكتب الأصوات الناقصة.

facts.en: Long ago English had its own special letters for th: þ (thorn) and ð (eth). When printing came to England about 550 years ago, the printers' letter sets came from Europe and had no thorn, so they wrote th instead.
facts.ar: قديماً كان للإنجليزية حرفان خاصان لصوت th هما þ وð. وعندما وصلت الطباعة إلى إنجلترا قبل نحو 550 سنة، جاءت حروف المطابع من أوروبا بلا هذين الحرفين، فصاروا يكتبون th بدلاً منهما.

facts.en: Sometimes printers used y for thorn. That is why old shop signs say 'Ye Olde Shop'. It was never 'ye' - it was 'the'!
facts.ar: أحياناً استخدم الطابعون الحرف y مكان thorn، ولهذا نرى لافتات قديمة مكتوب عليها Ye Olde Shop. لم تكن تُقرأ ye أبداً، بل the!

facts.en: ph comes from Greek words: phone, photo, elephant, alphabet. Greek had one letter for this sound: φ (phi). The word alphabet itself is alpha + beta, the first two Greek letters, just like Arabic أبجدية comes from أ ب ج د.
facts.ar: ph تأتي من كلمات يونانية مثل phone و photo و elephant و alphabet، وكان لليونانية حرف واحد لهذا الصوت هو φ. وكلمة alphabet نفسها من alpha + beta أول حرفين يونانيين، تماماً كما جاءت كلمة «أبجدية» من أ ب ج د.

facts.en: wh used to be written hw, and people really said h + w. Today most English speakers say just w: what, when, white.
facts.ar: كانت wh تُكتب قديماً hw ويُنطق فيها h ثم w. أما اليوم فمعظم المتحدثين ينطقونها w فقط: what و when و white.

arabicBridge.point: Same sound. Arabic gives it one letter; English needs two.
arabicBridge.pointAr: الصوت نفسه، لكن العربية تكتبه بحرف واحد والإنجليزية تحتاج حرفين.

arabicBridge.arabic: تش (وفي بعض لهجات الخليج والعراق: چ)
arabicBridge.point: Standard Arabic has no single letter for it; it is t + sh glued tightly together. Many Gulf speakers already say it in everyday words.
arabicBridge.pointAr: لا يوجد له حرف واحد في الفصحى، فهو t و sh ملتصقان بقوة. وكثير من أهل الخليج ينطقونه في كلامهم اليومي.

arabicBridge.english: th in think / th in this
arabicBridge.point: English writes both sounds the same way (th), but Arabic has two letters. Arabic speakers who use ث and ذ have an advantage over many other learners!
arabicBridge.pointAr: الإنجليزية تكتب الصوتين بالطريقة نفسها th، أما العربية فلها حرفان. ومن ينطق الثاء والذال جيداً عنده ميزة على كثير من متعلمي الإنجليزية!

arabicBridge.arabic: ثلاثة ← تلاتة، ذهب ← دهب، ذكي ← زكي
arabicBridge.point: In Egyptian colloquial, ث often becomes ت or س and ذ becomes د or ز. So Egyptian children may say 'tink', 'sink' or 'zis'. Use the Standard Arabic (Quran-reading) ث and ذ.
arabicBridge.pointAr: في العامية المصرية تصبح الثاء تاءً أو سيناً والذال دالاً أو زاياً، فقد يقول الطفل tink أو sink أو zis. استخدم الثاء والذال كما في الفصحى وقراءة القرآن.

arabicBridge.english: ph in phone, ck in duck, wh in what
arabicBridge.point: These digraphs make sounds Arabic already has. The only new thing is the spelling.
arabicBridge.pointAr: هذه الحروف المزدوجة تصنع أصواتاً موجودة في العربية؛ الجديد هو طريقة الكتابة فقط.

commonErrors.why: The child reads letter by letter. Detectives circle the digraph first and read it as one sound.
Colloquial Arabic (especially Egyptian) changes ث into س or ت. Tongue tip must peep out between the teeth.
Colloquial ذ becomes ز or د. Tongue out, plus throat buzz.
Spelling the sound with the wrong digraph or one letter. ph is mostly in Greek words; sh is the ش sound.
After a short vowel at the end of a short word, the k sound is spelled ck.

teacher: Detective badge image and a 'case file' slide for each digraph
Word cards: ship, shop, fish, dish, chip, chin, lunch, much, think, three, thank you, this, that, mother, brother, duck, back, sock, phone, photo, elephant, what, when, white
Old shop sign photo 'Ye Olde Shop' and the letter þ
student: A small mirror (or the camera self-view)
Paper, a pencil and a coloured pen for circling
A tissue for the th air test

stages.name: Warm-up: The Mystery Sound
stages.purpose: Set up the detective theme and recall sh and ch from Lesson 3.
teacherSays: Good morning, Spelling Detectives! Here is your badge. Today we solve a big mystery.
Listen: shhh! (Finger on lips.) What does it mean? Be quiet! Which letters write shhh?
Listen: ch-ch-ch, like a train! Which letters write it?
Mystery: shhh is ONE sound. But we write TWO letters. Why? Let's investigate!
teacherSaysAr: أهلاً يا محققي التهجئة! اليوم نحلّ لغزاً كبيراً.
shhh صوت واحد، لكننا نكتبه بحرفين. لماذا؟ هيا نحقق!
studentsDo: Make the 'quiet' sound and the 'train' sound with gestures (finger on lips, train arm).
Type or show the letters for each sound: sh, ch.
Say one word they remember from Lesson 3 with sh or ch.
tips: Keep it quick and dramatic: a whisper voice for the mystery works well.
Accept ship, fish, chip, chair from Lesson 3 as warm-up words.

stages.name: Discovery: Count the Sounds, Not the Letters
stages.method: Guided discovery with finger counting (phoneme segmentation) and sound boxes
stages.purpose: Discover that a digraph is two letters for one sound by comparing letter count and sound count.
teacherSays: Look: s-h-i-p. How many letters? Four. Now say it slowly and count with your fingers: sh... i... p. How many sounds? Three!
Four letters, three sounds. Two letters are holding hands to make ONE sound. We call them a digraph. Di means two, graph means writing.
Detective rule: first circle the letters that hold hands, then read.
Now you: fish. Letters? Sounds?
teacherSaysAr: حرفان يمسكان بيد بعضهما ليصنعا صوتاً واحداً: هذا هو الحرف المزدوج.
قاعدة المحقق: ضع دائرة حول الحرفين المتماسكين أولاً، ثم اقرأ.
studentsDo: Count letters (write the number) and sounds (show fingers) for each word.
Draw sound boxes: one box per sound, so the digraph shares one box.
Circle the digraph in each word with a coloured pen.

exercise.instructions: Write how many letters. Show how many sounds. Circle the digraph.
exercise.instructionsAr: اكتب عدد الحروف، وأرِني بأصابعك عدد الأصوات، وضع دائرة حول الحرف المزدوج.

tips: Children often count 4 sounds for ship at first. Say it very slowly with them and ask: did you hear an s and then an h? No - one sound.
Sound boxes can be drawn on paper and held up to the camera.

stages.name: Linguistics Corner: Why English Needs Digraphs
stages.nameAr: ركن اللغويات: لماذا تحتاج الإنجليزية الحروف المزدوجة؟
stages.method: Storytelling with images (history of writing) + quick quiz
stages.purpose: Understand where digraphs come from and widen general knowledge about alphabets.
teacherSays: Arabic has 28 letters. English has only 26 letters, but about 44 sounds! Not enough letters. So English makes teams.
Long ago, English had a special letter for th. Look: þ. Its name was thorn. Then printing machines came from Europe, and they had no thorn! So printers wrote t + h.
Look at this old sign: Ye Olde Shop. People think it says 'ye'. No! The y was a thorn. It says 'The Old Shop'!
ph comes from Greek: phone, photo, elephant. And the word alphabet? Alpha + beta, the first two Greek letters. Like أبجدية: أ ب ج د!
teacherSaysAr: الحروف الإنجليزية لا تكفي لكل الأصوات، فتصنع فِرَقاً من حرفين.
كلمة alphabet جاءت من أول حرفين في اليونانية، كما جاءت كلمة أبجدية من أ ب ج د.
studentsDo: Answer the quick quiz with thumbs up (true) or thumbs down (false).
Try to write the old letter þ on paper.
Say alphabet and أبجدية and spot the same idea.

exercise.instructions: True or false? Show thumbs up or thumbs down.
exercise.instructionsAr: صح أم خطأ؟ ارفع إبهامك لأعلى أو لأسفل.

items.prompt: English has more sounds than letters.
Long ago English had a letter called thorn for th.
'Ye Olde Shop' really means 'The Old Shop'.
ph in phone comes from Greek.
Arabic needs two letters to write ش.

tips: Keep the history to pictures and short sentences; the children only need to retell one fact.
The 'Ye Olde' story is a favourite to retell at home - push it as the fact of the day.

stages.name: Arabic Bridge: One Arabic Letter, Two English Letters
stages.nameAr: جسر العربية: حرف عربي واحد وحرفان إنجليزيان
stages.method: Contrastive analysis: matching English digraphs to Arabic letters
stages.purpose: Use Arabic letters as anchors for the digraph sounds and spot the sounds that need care.
teacherSays: Detectives, match the English team to the Arabic letter. sh = ش. Easy!
ch: Arabic has no single letter. It is t + sh glued fast: tsh! Some of you say چ at home, like چم. Same sound!
th is the clever one. Arabic has TWO letters: ث and ذ. English uses th for both!
ph = ف. ck = ك. wh = و. You already know these sounds - only the spelling is new.
teacherSaysAr: sh مثل الشين تماماً. و ch مثل «تش» ملتصقة.
th لها صوتان: مثل الثاء في think ومثل الذال في this.
ph تُنطق فاء، و ck كاف، و wh واو.
studentsDo: Draw a line on the slide from each digraph to its Arabic letter (or say the pair aloud).
Write the Arabic letter next to each digraph on paper.
Say a word for each: ship / شمس, chip / چاي (Gulf), think / ثلاثة, this / هذا.

exercise.instructions: Match the English digraph to the Arabic sound.
exercise.instructionsAr: صِل الحرف المزدوج الإنجليزي بالصوت العربي المناسب.

tips: If a child says 'chai' with چ, celebrate it: their dialect already has the English ch.
For Egyptian children, link th to Quran-reading ث and ذ, not to everyday تلاتة or دهب.

stages.name: The Th Twins: Think and This
stages.method: Multisensory articulation: mirror, tissue test and hand on throat
stages.purpose: Pronounce th correctly (tongue between teeth) and hear the voiceless and voiced th apart.
teacherSays: Mirror time! Put the tip of your tongue between your teeth. Just a little bit out. Blow: thhh. That is th in think, three, thank you.
Hold the tissue in front of your mouth: thhh - the tissue moves. No buzz in the throat. Like ث.
Now hand on throat: the, this, that, mother, brother. Buzz! Like ذ.
If your tongue stays inside, you say sink, not think! Tongue out, detectives!
teacherSaysAr: ضع طرف لسانك بين أسنانك. هذا هو th.
think بلا اهتزاز في الحلق مثل الثاء، و this مع اهتزاز مثل الذال.
studentsDo: Watch their tongue in the mirror for think, three, this, that.
Hand on throat: decide buzz or no buzz for each word.
Show a card: ث (no buzz) or ذ (buzz).
Say the chant: 'Thank you, thank you, three times thank you! This is my mother, that is my brother.'

exercise.instructions: Listen. Is th like ث (no buzz) or like ذ (buzz)? Show your card.
exercise.instructionsAr: استمع: هل th مثل الثاء (بلا اهتزاز) أم مثل الذال (مع اهتزاز)؟ ارفع البطاقة.

tips: Tell children it is polite and correct to show the tongue for th; some are shy about it.
Common pattern worth noticing: little words like the, this, that, they use the buzzing ذ sound.
th is taught fully in Lesson 5; today is a preview, so praise the tongue position more than perfect accuracy.

stages.name: Detective Case Files: Digraph Hunt and Sort
stages.nameAr: ملفات القضايا: صيد الحروف المزدوجة وتصنيفها
stages.method: Sound sorting game (word sort) + the ck detective rule (guided discovery)
stages.purpose: Recognise all six digraphs in words and discover when we spell k as ck.
teacherSays: New case! Each word hides a digraph. Find it and put the word in the right case file: sh, ch, th, ck, ph or wh.
Look at the ck words: duck, back, sock, neck. What comes just before ck? A short vowel: u, a, o, e! Detective rule: after a short vowel at the end of a short word, we write ck.
And the wh words: what, when, white. Question words love wh!
teacherSaysAr: كل كلمة تُخفي حرفاً مزدوجاً. جده وضع الكلمة في الملف الصحيح.
قاعدة: بعد حرف متحرك قصير في آخر الكلمة القصيرة نكتب ck.
studentsDo: Read each word, circle the digraph and say the case file (sh, ch, th, ck, ph, wh).
Race in pairs: who sorts the words first in the chat?
Find the pattern in the ck words and say the rule in English or Arabic.

exercise.instructions: Find the digraph. Put the word in the right case file.
exercise.instructionsAr: جد الحرف المزدوج وضع الكلمة في الملف الصحيح.

tips: phone, photo and white contain long vowels the children have not studied; tell them to focus only on the digraph.
Turn the fastest finisher into the 'chief detective' who checks the others' answers.

stages.name: Missing Letters: Crack the Code
stages.method: Spelling from sound (dictation with a gap) + peer checking
stages.purpose: Move from reading digraphs to spelling them.
teacherSays: I say a word. You write the missing digraph. Listen: ship. _ _ i p. Which two letters?
Check your partner's answer: is it correct? Detectives always check!
teacherSaysAr: أقول الكلمة وأنت تكتب الحرف المزدوج الناقص.
studentsDo: Write the full word on paper and hold it up to the camera.
Check a partner's answer and say 'Case closed!' when correct.

exercise.instructions: Listen and write the missing two letters.

tips: Pair the ship/chip items on purpose: same ending, different digraph.

stages.name: Exit Ticket, Did You Know? and Goodbye
stages.purpose: Check who can hear and spell digraphs alone, and send home one fact.
teacherSays: Exit ticket: I say five words. Write the digraph you hear.
Did you know? 'Ye Olde Shop' means 'The Old Shop'. The y was really an old letter for th!
Mission: find three things at home with sh, ch or th and teach your family the word 'digraph'.
teacherSaysAr: هل تعلم؟ عبارة Ye Olde Shop تعني The Old Shop، لأن y كانت حرفاً قديماً لصوت th!
مهمتك: جد ثلاثة أشياء في البيت فيها sh أو ch أو th.
studentsDo: Write the digraph for 5 words.
Say goodbye with a digraph word: 'Bye-bye, ship!'
tips: Note who scored under 4/5 and give them sh/ch/th word-reading in the warm-ups of Lessons 5-7.

exitTicket.instructions: Listen. Write the digraph you hear: sh, ch, th, ck, ph or wh.
exitTicket.instructionsAr: استمع واكتب الحرف المزدوج الذي تسمعه: sh أو ch أو th أو ck أو ph أو wh.

homework.en: Digraph Detective Notebook: find and write 6 words with digraphs (books, boxes, food packets at home). Circle the digraph in each word. Then tell your family the 'Ye Olde Shop' story.
homework.ar: دفتر المحقق: ابحث عن 6 كلمات فيها حروف مزدوجة (في الكتب والعلب وأغلفة الطعام في البيت) واكتبها وضع دائرة حول الحرف المزدوج. ثم احكِ لعائلتك قصة Ye Olde Shop.
tasks: Write 6 digraph words and circle the digraph.
Draw sound boxes for ship, chip and fish.
Say 'Thank you, this is my brother' in the mirror with your tongue out for th.

support: Work with sh and ch only (taught in Lesson 3) and add th at the end.
Give the Arabic letter as a hint card next to each digraph.
Let the child count sounds with counters or fingers before writing.
challenge: Find words with two digraphs: chick (ch + ck), shock (sh + ck), check (ch + ck), thick (th + ck).
Find a trigraph (three letters, one sound): tch in watch and match.
Spot more ph words: elephant, dolphin, alphabet.

successCriteria: Explains 'two letters, one sound' in English or Arabic with an example.
Counts letters and sounds correctly for at least 6 of 8 words.
Sorts at least 9 of 12 words into the right digraph file.
Puts the tongue between the teeth for th and shows voiceless vs voiced on at least 6 of 8 items.
watchFor: th said as s, t, z or d
k spelled k instead of ck after a short vowel (duk)

teacherNotes: Only sh and ch have been taught at this point. th, ck, ph and wh are a discovery preview: the goal is recognising the 'two letters, one sound' idea, not mastery.
th returns properly in Lesson 5 (with ng); refer back to the ث / ذ cards then.
phone, photo and white include long-vowel spellings taught later; read them for the children if needed and keep the focus on the digraph.
Keep the detective badge and the 'case file' slides: all four Level 2 Bonus Classes use the detective theme.
Bonus Class 2 moves from two letters for one sound to two sounds side by side: consonant clusters.
